name: partial_gap_fill_scalp_5s
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: Medium gaps (0.5%-1.5%) often partially fill (50-70% of the gap) before finding support/resistance. Rather than targeting a full gap fill, this strategy targets a partial fill — which has a higher probability of occurring. The partial fill level acts as a magnet because institutional VWAP algorithms anchor to the previous close, creating pull-back flow. Edge persists because most gap traders target full fills and get stopped out when the gap doesn't fully close.
mechanism: Opening gaps trigger stop-loss cascades from overnight position holders, overshooting fair value. As the cascade exhausts, institutional VWAP algorithms begin working counter-gap orders, and fresh participants enter at the perceived discount or premium, driving price back toward the prior close or VWAP level within the first 15-30 minutes.

filters.volume_filter: opening volume > 80% of 20-day avg opening volume

weaknesses: Opening slippage (4+ bps) eats into edge significantly
Partial fill target is arbitrary — 50% may not be the optimal level for all stocks
On strong momentum days, gap extends instead of filling even partially
prior_art: Gap fill with partial target — adaptation of classic gap fill to increase win rate
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
